statement.p: (a) Find a vector parallel to the line of intersection of the planes 5 x + 2 y - 5 z = 12 and -3 x + 2 y + 5 z = -6.
(b) Show that the point \left(1,1,-1\right) lies on both planes. Then find a vector parametric equation for the line of intersection.

static.solution:
(a) Normal vectors to the two planes are \vec n_1 = 5\vec i + 2 \vec j - 5 \vec k \quad \hbox{ and } \quad \vec n_2 = - 3\vec i + 2 \vec j + 5 \vec k. The vector \vec n_1\times\vec n_2 is perpendicular to both planes and parallel to the line of intersection: \vec n_1\times\vec n_2 = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ 5 \amp 2 \amp -5\\ -3 \amp 2 \amp 5 \end{array} \right| = 20\,\mathit{\vec i}-10\,\mathit{\vec j}+16\,\mathit{\vec k}.
(b) To check that the point \left(1,1,-1\right) lies on the planes, substitute into each equation. 5 x + 2 y - 5 z = (5)(1) + (2)(1) + (-5)(-1) = 12, and -3 x + 2 y + 5 z = (-3)(1) + (2)(1) + (5)(-1) = -6. Thus, the point lies on both planes. Then a vector parametric equation of the line is \vec r(t) = \left(1+20t\right)\,\mathit{\vec i}+\left(1-10t\right)\,\mathit{\vec j}+\left(16t-1\right)\,\mathit{\vec k}.
